questions.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+3y \\ 2x-y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & -14 & -14\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 7 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{9}{4} \\ -\frac{7}{4} & -\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
Let $B={{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}$ be a basis of ${R}^{3}.$ The matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ is given by

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & b & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & c\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}+3{b}_{3}, \\ T({b}_{2}) & ={b}_{1}+3{b}_{2}, \\ T({b}_{3}) & =2{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2}+3{b}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write down the coordinates of the images relative to the basis $B:$

$$
[T({b}_{1})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{2})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,[T({b}_{3})]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, the $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix  whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=2,$ $b=3,$ $c=3$ and 

$$
a+b+c=2+3+3=8.
$$

questions.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 & b & 4 \\ a & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 10\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & 3 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 2 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -7 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=-7,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=1+(-7)+2=-4.
$$

questions.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}6x-7y \\ -2x-6y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}6 \\ -2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}50 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 50 & 10 \\ -2 & 2 & 0 & -20\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{6}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{25}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ -2 & 2 & 0 & -20\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{25}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & \frac{10}{3} & \frac{50}{3} & -\frac{50}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:=\frac{3}{10}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{25}{3} & \frac{5}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & -5\end{aligned}].
$$

questions.problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & b & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}x+y+z \\ x+z \\ y-z\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1},$ ${b}_{2},$ and ${b}_{3}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{3}) & =T([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1}),$ $T({b}_{2}),$ and $T({b}_{3})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & {b}_{3} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) & T({b}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & -1 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 & -3 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:=2{R}_{2}+{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 & -5 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -5 & -9 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 1 & \frac{4}{3} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a=-5,$ $b=3,$ $c=2$ and 

$$
a+b+c=-5+3+2=0.
$$
